# TempleCBE

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE/actions)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE)
[![License: GPL-3 \|
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL--3%20%7C%20MIT-yellow.svg)](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/LICENSE.md)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/yaml?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fjkylearmstrong%2FTempleCBE%2Fmaster%2FDESCRIPTION&query=%24.Version&label=version&color=blue)](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE)

**TempleCBE** is an open-source clinical data science, biostatistical
modeling, and pipeline orchestration framework developed for Temple
University’s **Center for Biostatistics and Epidemiology (CBE)** at the
Lewis Katz School of Medicine and College of Public Health.

`TempleCBE` bridges the critical methodology gap between **classical
regulatory biostatistics** (SAS numerical parity, exact contingency
inference, counting-process survival analysis), **modern machine
learning** (`tidymodels`, penalized Cox regression, joint
survival-status-time ensembles, Python `reticulate` export), and
**automated clinical pipeline orchestration** (multi-table databases,
Excel round-trips, DAG dependency tracking).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🎯 Which Gap Areas Does TempleCBE Cover?

Clinical research and biostatistical pipelines often face tooling
fragmentation across language boundaries, regulatory standards, and
modeling ecosystems. `TempleCBE` directly addresses six foundational gap
areas:

| \# | Methodology Gap Area | The Clinical & Modeling Problem | How `TempleCBE` Fills the Gap | Dedicated Vignette |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **1** | **Start/Stop Counting-Process Data** | Time-varying longitudinal covariates (`Surv(tstart, tstop, status)`) suffer interval leakage when events occur between scheduled visits; standard tools flatten or crash on counting-process matrices. | [`tidy_tmerge_cox()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/tidy_tmerge_cox.md) constructs verified counting intervals; [`get_dataset_info()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/get_dataset_info.md) audits counting-process duration and events without matrix flattening; [`cv_coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cv_coxnet.md) enforces subject-grouped partitioning to prevent cross-fold leakage. | [Nested Survival CV](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/nested_survival_cv.html) & [SAS Survival](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/sas_survival.html) |
| **2** | **Tidymodels & Survival ML** | `tidymodels` and `censored` lack specialized clinical recipes (supervised likelihood encoding for survival, mixed-data FAMD) and calibrated multi-paradigm ensembles for complex clinical risk prediction. | S3 `hardhat` engines ([`coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/coxnet.md), [`cv_coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cv_coxnet.md)), custom recipe steps ([`step_lencode_coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/step_lencode_coxnet.md), [`step_famd()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/step_famd.md)), a `coxnet` engine for [`parsnip::proportional_hazards()`](https://parsnip.tidymodels.org/reference/proportional_hazards.html) that also accepts start/stop outcomes, LOCO mini-patch inference ([`loco_mp_coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/loco_mp_coxnet.md)), and stacked joint ensembles ([`joint_model()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/joint_model.md)). | [Nested Survival CV](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/nested_survival_cv.html) |
| **3** | **SAS Regulatory Parity & Validation** | Migrating FDA/regulatory trials between SAS and R leads to discrepancies in `PROC PHREG`, `PROC COMPARE`, `PROC PRINCOMP`, zero-cell Fisher exact conservatism, and non-standard missing codes (`999`, `-99`). | [`compare_df()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/compare_df.md) gives a tidy cell-level comparison that agrees with SAS `PROC COMPARE` on a committed SAS 9.4 benchmark (differences are listed in [`?compare_df`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/compare_df.md)); [`run_pca()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/run_pca.md) reproduces exact `PROC PRINCOMP` eigenvalue tables; [`exact2x2()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/exact2x2.md) provides automatic mid-p exact testing; automated SAS macro bridges ([`run_sas_script()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/run_sas_script.md)). | [R to SAS](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/R_to_SAS.html) & [PCA Analysis](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/pca_analysis.html) |
| **4** | **Python & Reticulate Cross-Language ML** | Advanced survival ML, SHAP explanations, and deep learning live in Python, while clinical data wrangling and biostatistical models live in R. | Seamless two-way `reticulate` serialization, exporting fitted R models, survival components, and data dictionaries directly into Python environments (`DALEXtra`, `survex`, `scikit-learn`). | [Reticulate Export](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/reticulate_export.html) |
| **5** | **Multi-Table Clinical Databases & ER Graphs** | Clinical datasets arrive as multi-table relational lists (`inputs`, `ABG`, `Cardiovascular`, `survival_data`). Managing consolidated dictionaries, Excel sheets, variable roles, and cohort overlap requires tedious boilerplate. | Consolidated multi-table [`get_dataset_info.list()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/get_dataset_info.md), multi-sheet Excel export/import ([`write_database_to_excel()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/write_database_to_excel.md), [`read_database_from_excel()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/read_database_from_excel.md)), in-place metadata sync ([`apply_database_metadata()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/apply_database_metadata.md)), variable role management ([`variable_roles()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/variable_roles.md)), and Entity-Relationship graph analysis ([`database_relationships()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/database_relationships.md), [`cbe_database_venn()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cbe_database_venn.md)). | [EDA & Missingness](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/eda_and_missingness.html) |
| **6** | **Pipeline DAGs & Reproducible Reporting** | Multi-report analytical deliverables lack lightweight dependency tracking without configuring heavyweight workflow managers like Make or Snakemake. | [`compute_graph()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/compute_graph.md) tracks script, data, and report dependencies as typed DAGs; `as_tbl_graph()` / [`as_igraph()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/as_igraph.md) converts to standard networks; [`render_pipeline()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/render_pipeline.md) executes staleness-aware compilation of Quarto/Rmd deliverables. | [Compute Graph](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/compute_graph.html) |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🏷️ Function Naming Convention (`cbe_*`)

TempleCBE follows a clear and consistent functional naming rule: -
**`cbe_*`** is reserved for **Temple CBE presentation and formatting
only** (themes, palettes, scales, plots, report tables, and number
formatters such as
[`cbe_theme_survival()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cbe_theme_survival.md),
[`cbe_palette()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cbe_palette.md),
[`cbe_contingency_plot()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cbe_contingency_plot.md),
[`cbe_cox_table()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cbe_cox_table.md),
[`cbe_pformat()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/pformat.md)). -
**All other functions** are plain verb-noun identifiers that directly
describe their computational action
(e.g. [`nested_survival_run()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/nested_survival_run.md),
[`cox_single()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cox_single.md),
[`checkpoint_map()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/checkpoint_map.md),
[`describe_columns()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/get_dataset_info.md),
[`drop_correlated_columns()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/drop_correlated_columns.md),
[`tune_alpha_by_split()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/tune_alpha_by_split.md),
[`docx_review_extract()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/docx_review_extract.md)). -
The legacy non-formatting `cbe_*` names (deprecated in 0.5.8) were
removed in 0.7.0;
[`find_deprecated_calls()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/find_deprecated_calls.md)
finds them in your code.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 📦 Installation

Install the development version directly from GitHub:

``` r

# Install pak if not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")

# Install TempleCBE
pak::pak("jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE")
```

Or via `remotes`:

``` r

remotes::install_github("jkylearmstrong/TempleCBE")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🚀 Key Feature Showcases

``` r

library(TempleCBE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)
```

### 1. Multi-Table Clinical Databases & Relational Linkage

Manage multi-domain clinical trial databases (e.g. baseline inputs,
serial labs, and survival endpoints), compile unified data dictionaries,
and evaluate entity-relationship linkages:

``` r

# 1. Define multi-table database list
clinical_db <- list(
  inputs        = data.frame(patient_id = 1:5, age = c(45, 52, 61, 39, 48), sex = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "M")),
  ABG           = data.frame(patient_id = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3), ph = c(7.35, 7.40, 7.28, 7.32, 7.45)),
  survival_data = data.frame(patient_id = 1:5, surv = Surv(c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50), c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1)))
)

# 2. Assign database metadata and dataset descriptions
database_name(clinical_db) <- "CardioPulmonaryTrial"
clinical_db <- set_dataset_labels(clinical_db, list(
  inputs = "Baseline Demographics",
  ABG = "Serial Arterial Blood Gas",
  survival_data = "Time-to-Event Clinical Followup"
))

# 3. Consolidated data dictionary across all tables
get_dataset_info(clinical_db, subject_id = "patient_id")

# 4. Multi-sheet Excel workbook export with automated METADATA worksheet
write_database_to_excel(clinical_db, "Clinical_Trial_Database.xlsx")

# 5. Entity-Relationship graph & cohort overlap analysis
rel <- database_relationships(clinical_db)
as_tbl_graph(rel) # Convert directly to tidygraph
cbe_database_venn(clinical_db, id_col = "patient_id") # Visual Venn overlap
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 2. Dataset Comparison (Checked Against SAS `PROC COMPARE`) & Visual Concordance

Audit dataset concordance down to the individual cell with
tolerance-based matching and 2-set Venn visualizations. The counts and
differences agree with SAS 9.4 `PROC COMPARE` (`METHOD=ABSOLUTE`) on the
nine small comparisons of `inst/sas/benchmark_proc_compare.sas`; where
they differ (the sign of a difference, variables of different types,
trailing blanks, R classes against SAS types, attributes other than the
type) is listed in
[`?compare_df`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/compare_df.md):

``` r

df_base <- data.frame(id = 1:5, age = c(45, 52, 60, 65, 70), stage = c("I", "II", "II", "III", "IV"))
df_comp <- data.frame(id = 1:5, age = c(45, 52, 62, 65, 70), stage = c("I", "II", "II", "III", "IV"))

# Cell-level comparison, modelled on SAS PROC COMPARE
cmp <- compare_df(df_base, df_comp, by = "id", base_name = "Base", compare_name = "Audit")
print(cmp)

# Visual diagnostic: Observation and Variable Venn diagrams
autoplot(cmp, type = "observations")
autoplot(cmp, type = "discrepancies")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 3. Penalized Cox Models for Start/Stop & Longitudinal Data (`tidymodels`)

[`coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/coxnet.md)
and
[`cv_coxnet()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cv_coxnet.md)
provide a `tidymodels`-native `hardhat` interface for regularized Cox
regression with subject-grouped cross-validation. Outcomes can be
right-censored, `Surv(time, status)`, or start/stop counting-process
data, `Surv(tstart, tstop, status)`, for time-varying covariates:

``` r

lung_clean <- na.omit(lung[, c("time", "status", "age", "sex", "ph.ecog")])

# Fit elastic-net penalized Cox model
fit_cox <- coxnet(Surv(time, status) ~ ., data = lung_clean, penalty = 0.05, mixture = 0.5)

# Subject-grouped Cross-Validation with Integrated Brier Score
cv_fit <- cv_coxnet(Surv(time, status) ~ ., data = lung_clean, v = 5)
generics::tidy(cv_fit)

# Start/stop data (`long`: one row per subject-interval): folds keep each subject's intervals together
cv_ss <- cv_coxnet(
  Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ x1 + x2, data = long,
  subject_id = "subject_id", v = 5
)
```

A `penalty` below the end of glmnet’s default path is honored (the path
is continued down to it; `penalty = 0` is the unpenalized fit) rather
than silently clamped. `coxnet` is also registered as an engine of
[`parsnip::proportional_hazards()`](https://parsnip.tidymodels.org/reference/proportional_hazards.html),
so it works in workflows and
[`tune::tune_grid()`](https://tune.tidymodels.org/reference/tune_grid.html):

``` r

spec <- parsnip::proportional_hazards(penalty = 0.05, mixture = 0.5) |>
  parsnip::set_engine("coxnet")
fit <- parsnip::fit(spec, Surv(time, status) ~ ., data = lung_clean)
predict(fit, lung_clean[1:3, ], type = "survival", eval_time = c(180, 365))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 4. Joint Survival-Status-Time Modeling

[`joint_model()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/joint_model.md)
fits penalized Cox proportional hazards, calibrated binary event
classification, and follow-up duration regression together, and predicts
all three side by side:

``` r

# Fit the multi-paradigm joint model
jm_fit <- joint_model(
  lung_clean,
  Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog,
  engine = "glmnet"
)

# Multi-horizon dynamic survival predictions
predict(jm_fit, lung_clean[1:5, ], eval_time = c(180, 365))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 5. Principal Component Analysis (SAS `PROC PRINCOMP` Parity)

[`run_pca()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/run_pca.md)
executes standardized PCA and outputs the exact eigenvalue variance
table produced by SAS `PROC PRINCOMP`:

``` r

# Standardized PCA on continuous variables
iris_pca <- run_pca(iris[, 1:4], scale = TRUE)

# 1. Scree plot with Kaiser-Guttman threshold (Eigenvalue >= 1)
pca_scree_plot(iris_pca, metric = "eigenvalue", kaiser = TRUE)

# 2. Variable correlation circle on unit circle
pca_variables_plot(iris_pca, x = 1, y = 2)

# 3. Loadings biplot with 95% concentration ellipses
pca_biplot(iris_pca, group = iris$Species, ellipse = TRUE, percent = TRUE)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 6. Pipeline Dependency & Computational Graph Tracking

Model analysis scripts and data deliverables as an interactive DAG:

``` r

# Define pipeline stages and track downstream artifacts
graph <- compute_graph(
  stages = list(
    data_clean = list(inputs = "raw.csv", outputs = "clean.rds"),
    model_fit  = list(inputs = "clean.rds", outputs = "model.rds")
  )
)

# Generate staleness-aware execution plan
get_render_plan(graph)
```

## 📚 Comprehensive Vignettes

`TempleCBE` includes extensive vignettes covering theory, simulation,
and clinical workflows:

| \# | Vignette Title | Key Topics & Methodology |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **01** | [Exploratory Data Analysis, Missingness Auditing, and Normalization](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/eda_and_missingness.html) | Multi-code missing sentinels, missingness maps, IQR fences, and multi-table clinical database dictionaries. |
| **02** | [Penalized Cox Models and Nested Cross-Validation](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/nested_survival_cv.html) | Start/stop counting process data, subject-level partitioning, `step_lencode_coxnet`, and yardstick survival scoring. |
| **03** | [Visualizing Computational Pipeline Dependencies](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/compute_graph.html) | Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), multi-report orchestration, and reproducible analysis plans. |
| **04** | [Validation Guide for SAS Users: Cox Models](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/sas_survival.html) | Cross-validating [`cox_single()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cox_single.md), [`cox_multi()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/cox_multi.md), and [`tidy_tmerge_cox()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/tidy_tmerge_cox.md) against SAS `PROC PHREG`. |
| **05** | [Cross-Validating Advanced Survival Models: R to SAS](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/R_to_SAS.html) | Automated macro exports, macro validation suites, `cbe_compare_df` verification, and numerical concordance benchmarks. |
| **06** | [Multi-Language Interoperability and Python Pipelines](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/reticulate_export.html) | Reticulate bridges, exporting survival matrices and models to Python (`DALEXtra`, `survex`), and cross-language artifact transfer. |
| **07** | [Principal Component Analysis in R and SAS](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/articles/pca_analysis.html) | SAS `PROC PRINCOMP` eigenvalue parity, Kaiser-Guttman scree plots, biplots, and clinical TAS dimension reduction. |

Access any vignette locally after installation via:

``` r

vignette("nested_survival_cv", package = "TempleCBE")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🏛️ Ecosystem Architecture

`TempleCBE` serves as the public, auditable methodological layer of
Temple University CBE’s clinical data science framework. Protected
institutional studies and EHR analyses import `TempleCBE` to ensure
statistical rigor while keeping confidential patient data secure:

- **[`pslongSim`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/pslongSim)**:
  Longitudinal propensity score simulation engine generating synthetic
  benchmark cohorts.
- **[`omop-duck-db`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong/omop-duck-db)**:
  High-performance OMOP Common Data Model querying with DuckDB.
- **[`quarto_temple_brand`](https://github.com/jkylearmstrong-temple/quarto_temple_brand)**:
  Official Temple University institutional Quarto document and slide
  deck templates.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🛡️ Rigorous Code Audit & v0.5.0 Release

In preparation for the v0.5.0 release, `TempleCBE` underwent an
exhaustive, multi-tiered code and statistical audit addressing 137
verified findings across data privacy, numerical accuracy,
cross-platform containment, and survival methodology:

- **Data Privacy & De-Identification**: Hardened identifier
  pseudonymization (the keyed HMAC methods now require a secret key and
  warn on short keys), synthetic investigator names sampled from the 250
  most common US Census surnames and a pool of common first names, and
  automated redaction in multi-reviewer DOCX review tracking.
- **Statistical Integrity & Parity**: Smoke tests on five classic
  cohorts from R’s `survival` package (`veteran`, `lung`, `rotterdam`,
  `heart`, `colon`) check that fits and predictions run and return
  well-formed output. SAS parity is checked against committed reference
  numbers printed by SAS 9.4 for `PROC PHREG` (the counting-process
  tumor data and the `lung` cohort), `PROC PRINCOMP` (the eigenvalue
  table of
  [`run_pca()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/run_pca.md)
  on `iris`), `PROC COMPARE`
  ([`compare_df()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/compare_df.md)
  on nine small comparisons) and the IPCW Brier score and integrated
  Brier score macro; re-running SAS itself is opt-in
  (`TEMPLECBE_RUN_SAS_TESTS`) and needs a SAS installation.
- **Accelerated Racing Workflows**: Integrated `finetune` ANOVA and
  win-loss racing interfaces
  ([`control_race_survival()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/control_race_survival.md),
  [`tune_race_survival()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/tune_race_survival.md))
  for fast hyperparameter optimization of penalized survival models and
  joint ensembles.
- **Clean Canonical CBE API**: Refactored core functions to canonical
  names (`km_single`, `cox_multi`, `compare_df`, etc.) with full
  backwards-compatible `cbe_*` aliases.
- **Zero-Leakage Assurance**: Before each release a private list of
  terms that must not appear is checked against every tracked file and
  the extracted text of tracked PDFs (`test-denylist.R`; it runs only
  where that private list is available, so it is a release check, not
  part of CI).

# Package index

## Data Quality & Missingness Analysis

Functions for missing data auditing, summary tables, and visualizations.

- [`count_na()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/count_na.md)
  : Count Total Missing (NA) Values
- [`features_percent_miss()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/features_percent_miss.md)
  : Calculate Percentage of Missing Data Per Feature
- [`plot(`*`<features_percent_miss>`*`)`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/plot_features_percent_miss.md)
  [`plot_features_percent_miss()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/plot_features_percent_miss.md)
  : Plot method for features_percent_miss objects
- [`missmap()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/missmap.md)
  : Missingness Map
- [`add_missing()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/add_missing.md)
  : Add Missing Values Completely at Random
- [`summary_table()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/summary_table.md)
  : Summary Table Function
- [`get_dataset_info()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/get_dataset_info.md)
  [`describe_columns()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/get_dataset_info.md)
  : Summarize a Data Frame or Joint Model's Columns and Components
- [`compare_df()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/compare_df.md)
  : Compare Two Data Frames (Modelled on SAS PROC COMPARE)
- [`autoplot(`*`<cbe_compare_df>`*`)`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/autoplot.cbe_compare_df.md)
  : Autoplot Method for CBE Data Frame Comparison
- [`reconcile_column_dictionary()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/reconcile_column_dictionary.md)
  : Reconcile a Data Frame's Column Names With a Column Dictionary

## Clinical Databases & Multi-Table Management

Functions for multi-table clinical databases, metadata export/import,
variable role assignment, and relational linkage analysis.

- [`dataset_label()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`` `dataset_label<-`() ``](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`database_name()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`` `database_name<-`() ``](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`database_label()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`` `database_label<-`() ``](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`set_dataset_labels()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  [`get_dataset_labels()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/dataset_labels.md)
  : Get or Set Dataset and Database Labels
- [`write_database_to_excel()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/write_database_to_excel.md)
  [`write_workbook()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/write_database_to_excel.md)
  [`write_database()`](https://jkylearmstrong.github.io/TempleCBE/reference/write_database_to_excel.md)

functions do not de-identify dates, record numbers, or free text.
